scenario: You work part-time at a neighborhood grocery store, usually on Saturday mornings. Starting next month, you will be volunteering as a swimming instructor for children every Saturday morning. Your coworker Dana has said she would happily trade her Wednesday evening shift for yours, but all permanent schedule changes need the store manager's approval.
to: Ms. Carla Benson, grocery store manager
subject: Request to switch my Saturday shift
bullets: Explain why you want to change your shift.
Describe the arrangement you have discussed with your coworker.
Ask for approval and offer to help during the transition.
sample_response:
Dear Ms. Benson,

I hope you are doing well. I am writing to ask whether I could permanently change my regular Saturday morning shift. Starting on March 4, I will be teaching free swimming lessons to children at the Riverside Community Pool every Saturday from 8 a.m. to noon, which directly overlaps with my current hours.

Fortunately, I have already talked with Dana Morales, who works the Wednesday evening shift from 5 to 10 p.m. She told me she would actually prefer weekend mornings, so we would simply trade shifts. Since we have both been trained on the register and at the deli counter, the store would not lose any coverage.

If you approve this change, I would be glad to work both shifts during the first week so that Dana and I can make sure nothing is missed. I could also update the shift notes for her. Please let me know if you would like to discuss this in person.

Thank you for considering my request.

Best regards,
Jamal

scenario: You recently started a small English–Spanish language exchange group that meets every week in a crowded café. The group has grown to about twelve members, and it is now too noisy to have real conversations. You have heard that the Maple Street Public Library has meeting rooms that community groups can reserve.
to: Mr. Thomas Reid, community services librarian
subject: Reserving a meeting room for a language group
bullets: Describe your group and its activities.
Explain why you are looking for a new place to meet.
Ask about the rules and process for booking a room.
sample_response:
Dear Mr. Reid,

My name is Hana, and I organize a language exchange group for people who want to practice English and Spanish. We meet every Thursday from 6:30 to 8 p.m. Members spend the first half of each session speaking one language and the second half speaking the other, and we sometimes play vocabulary games or discuss short news articles.

Until now, we have met at a café on Elm Avenue, but the group has grown to about twelve people. Between the coffee machines and the loud music, we can barely hear each other, which defeats the whole purpose of practicing conversation.

A friend mentioned that the library offers meeting rooms to community groups, so I would like to know more. Is there a fee for nonprofit groups, and how far in advance should I reserve a room? I would also like to know whether we could book the same time every week.

Thank you very much for your help.

Kind regards,
Hana

scenario: Your home internet connection has been dropping several times a day for two weeks. The internet provider scheduled a technician visit for last Tuesday, so you stayed home from work all morning, but no one came and no one called. You are still paying the full monthly fee for the service.
to: Customer Care Team, Brightline Internet
subject: Missed technician appointment and ongoing outages
bullets: Describe the problem with your internet service.
Explain what happened with the technician appointment.
Say what you expect the company to do now.
sample_response:
Dear Customer Care Team,

I am writing to complain about the service on my account, number 448210. For the past two weeks, my internet connection has been cutting out four or five times a day, usually for ten to twenty minutes. Because I sometimes work from home, these interruptions have caused me to drop out of video meetings more than once.

When I reported the problem, your company scheduled a technician visit for last Tuesday between 8 a.m. and noon. I took the morning off work and waited at home, but nobody arrived, and I received no call or message explaining the delay. That cost me half a day of vacation for nothing.

I would like a technician to visit this week at a confirmed time, preferably on Thursday or Friday afternoon. I also expect a credit on my bill for the days the service has not worked properly. I look forward to your prompt reply.

Sincerely,
Marcus Webb

scenario: You started a part-time job at the front desk of a small hotel a month ago. Your coworker Ben spent extra time teaching you how to use the booking system and handle difficult guests. Next week, you will work your first night shift alone, and you are a little nervous about it.
to: Ben Carter, coworker at the hotel front desk
subject: Thanks for all your help
bullets: Thank him for training you.
Give an example of how his advice helped you.
Ask for tips about working the night shift.
sample_response:
Hi Ben,

I just wanted to say a big thank you for everything you've taught me this month. You never seemed annoyed when I asked the same question about the booking system for the third time, and you always explained things patiently, even on busy weekends.

Your advice really paid off last Saturday. A guest arrived late and was furious because his room wasn't ready. I remembered what you told me: stay calm, apologize first, and offer something concrete. I gave him a free breakfast voucher and found him a room with a better view, and he actually thanked me before going upstairs!

As you know, I'm working my first night shift alone next Friday, and I'm a bit nervous. Since you've done plenty of them, could you share a few tips? For example, what usually happens after midnight, and who should I call if something goes wrong?

Thanks again. Coffee is on me next time!

Cheers,
Lily

scenario: Your aunt Margaret has invited you to spend the first week of July at her lake house with the rest of the family. You love these gatherings, but you have just accepted a summer internship at an architecture firm that begins on July 1. You don't want her to think you don't care about the family.
to: Aunt Margaret, your aunt
subject: About the first week of July
bullets: Thank her for the invitation.
Explain why you cannot come.
Suggest another way to spend time with the family this summer.
sample_response:
Dear Aunt Margaret,

Thank you so much for inviting me to the lake house in July. Whenever I think of those summers, I remember canoeing with my cousins and eating your famous blueberry pancakes, so your invitation made me smile.

Unfortunately, I won't be able to join you this year. I've just accepted a summer internship at Hartley & Moss, an architecture firm downtown, and my first day is July 1. As a new intern, I really can't ask for time off during the first week, especially since they've planned a full orientation program for us. I'm sad to miss it, but this internship is a big step toward the career I want.

That said, I'd love to see everyone before the summer ends. Would you mind if I drove up for the long weekend in August? I could bring dessert and help with the cooking. Please give my love to everyone at the lake.

With love,
Sophie

scenario: You have a small plot in your neighborhood's community garden. During the recent hot weather, several shared plants, such as the herbs near the entrance, dried out because no one was responsible for watering them. The garden coordinator, Mr. Hughes, has said that members can share ideas with him at any time.
to: Mr. Walter Hughes, community garden coordinator
subject: A suggestion for watering the shared plants
bullets: Describe the problem you have noticed.
Suggest a solution.
Offer to help put your idea into practice.
sample_response:
Dear Mr. Hughes,

I hope your tomatoes survived the heat wave better than ours did! I'm writing because I've noticed a problem with the shared plants near the garden entrance. During the last two weeks of hot weather, the basil, mint, and rosemary there turned brown and dry. I think each of us assumed someone else was watering them, so in the end nobody did.

I'd like to suggest a simple rotating schedule. Each member could sign up for one day a week to water the shared beds, and we could post the list on the tool shed door along with a short checklist. With around thirty members, nobody would need to volunteer more than once or twice a month.

If you like this idea, I'd be happy to create the schedule and send a sign-up message to everyone on the email list. I could also replant the herbs this weekend.

Thanks for all the work you do for the garden.

Best wishes,
Nadia

scenario: Last Saturday, you hosted a birthday party at your house. Two of your guests parked in front of your neighbor's driveway, and Mrs. Kowalski could not get her car out to go to an appointment. She left a polite but clearly upset note on your door the next morning.
to: Mrs. Irene Kowalski, neighbor
subject: My apologies for Saturday night
bullets: Apologize for what happened.
Explain how the problem occurred.
Describe what you will do to prevent it from happening again.
sample_response:
Dear Mrs. Kowalski,

Thank you for your note, and please accept my sincere apologies for what happened on Saturday evening. I was very sorry to learn that you couldn't get your car out and missed your appointment because of my guests. That must have been extremely frustrating.

I'm afraid it was my fault. More people came to the party than I had expected, and the street filled up quickly. I should have told everyone where to park, but I was busy in the kitchen and didn't check outside. Two friends who had never visited before simply didn't notice your driveway in the dark.

In the future, I will ask guests to park in the lot behind the pharmacy on Grove Street, and I'll go outside myself to check the street during any gathering. I'll also let you know in advance whenever I'm expecting visitors.

Again, I'm truly sorry. I hope you'll accept a small apple pie as a peace offering this weekend.

Warm regards,
Daniel

scenario: You have booked three nights at a small hotel for a trip to a coastal city next month. Your flight lands at 7 a.m., but the hotel's website says check-in begins at 3 p.m. You would also like to know the best way to get from the airport to the hotel.
to: Reservations Desk, Harbor View Inn
subject: Questions about my upcoming stay
bullets: Give the details of your reservation.
Ask about checking in early or storing your luggage.
Ask for advice about transportation from the airport.
sample_response:
Dear Reservations Team,

I have a reservation at the Harbor View Inn for three nights, from May 12 to May 15, under the name Kevin Tran. The confirmation number is HV20731, and I booked a double room with a sea view.

I have a question about my arrival. My flight lands at 7 a.m. on May 12, so I will probably reach the hotel around 9 a.m., long before your usual check-in time of 3 p.m. Would it be possible to check in early, even for an extra fee? If no room is ready, could I leave my suitcase at the front desk while I explore the old town?

I would also appreciate some advice about getting from the airport. Is there a shuttle bus or train that stops near the hotel, or would you recommend a taxi? If you know the approximate cost and travel time, that would be very helpful.

Thank you in advance for your help. I am really looking forward to my stay.

Best regards,
Kevin Tran

scenario: You subscribe to a weekly meal-kit service that delivers boxes of fresh ingredients every Monday. Because of your new work schedule, you are now away from home on Mondays until late at night, and last week your box sat outside all day and the food spoiled. You would like to keep the service.
to: Customer Support, FreshTable Meal Kits
subject: Changing my delivery day
bullets: Explain what happened to your last delivery.
Describe why the current delivery day no longer works.
Propose a solution and ask how to arrange it.
sample_response:
Hello FreshTable Support Team,

I've been a happy subscriber for about eight months, but I ran into a problem last week. My Monday box was delivered at around 10 a.m. and left outside my apartment door. By the time I got home at 9 p.m., the chicken and yogurt were warm, and I had to throw most of the ingredients away.

The issue is that my schedule has changed. I recently started a new job that requires me to work long shifts at a warehouse on Mondays and Tuesdays, so nobody is home to bring the box inside on those days.

I'd like to move my delivery to Thursday, when I'm usually home all afternoon. If that's not possible, could you deliver to my building's front office instead? Could you also tell me how to update this in my account, and whether I might receive a partial credit for last week's spoiled box?

Thanks very much,
Aisha

scenario: Your younger cousin Mateo, who is seventeen, wrote to ask for your advice. He has been offered two summer jobs: working as a counselor at a children's camp or working as a cashier at a busy café. You had a similar choice a few years ago and remember what you learned.
to: Mateo, your cousin
subject: Re: Which summer job should I take?
bullets: Respond to his request for advice.
Recommend one of the jobs and give reasons.
Share a tip from your own experience.
sample_response:
Hey Mateo,

Congratulations on getting two job offers! That's impressive, and it's great that you're thinking carefully before choosing. I'm glad you asked me, because I faced almost the same decision when I was your age.

Honestly, I'd go with the camp counselor job. The café would probably pay a little more, but the camp will teach you skills that look great on a college application, like leadership, problem-solving, and taking responsibility for other people. You'll also spend most of the day outdoors instead of standing behind a counter, and you'll make friends with the other counselors very quickly.

One tip from my own summer at Pine Lake Camp: bring more energy than you think you'll need, and don't be afraid to ask the older counselors for help. The first week was exhausting, and I almost quit, but by the end I didn't want to leave.

Whatever you decide, let me know how it goes!

Talk soon,
Andrea

scenario: You have been renting an apartment for six months, and you work from home three days a week. The spare bedroom has bare white walls and no storage, so you would like to paint one wall and put up shelves. Your lease says tenants need the landlord's written permission before making any changes.
to: Mr. Gregory Hall, landlord
subject: Permission to paint and install shelves
bullets: Describe the changes you would like to make.
Explain why these changes are important to you.
Explain how you will make sure the apartment is not damaged.
sample_response:
Dear Mr. Hall,

I hope you are well. I am writing to ask for your written permission to make two small changes to the spare bedroom in my apartment, unit 4B. I would like to paint one wall a light sage green and install three wooden shelves above the desk.

Since I now work from home three days a week, I use that room as my office. At the moment, my files and books are stacked on the floor, which makes the space feel cluttered and makes it hard to concentrate. A calmer color and proper storage would make it a much more comfortable place to work.

I will hire a licensed handyman, whose details I can send you, to mount the shelves securely. When I move out, I will remove the shelves, fill the holes, and repaint the wall white at my own expense, so the room will be returned in its original condition.

Thank you for considering my request.

Sincerely,
Olivia

scenario: You just finished an eight-week adult swimming course at your city's recreation center. The center has asked participants to send feedback by email. You thought the instructor was excellent, but the pool was often so crowded with other swimmers that your class had little space to practice.
to: Ms. Joanne Price, recreation center program director
subject: Feedback on the adult swimming course
bullets: Describe what you liked about the course.
Explain one problem you experienced.
Suggest how the course could be improved.
sample_response:
Dear Ms. Price,

Thank you for the chance to share my thoughts on the adult beginner swimming course, which I completed last week. Overall, it was a wonderful experience. Our instructor, Mr. Alvarez, was patient and encouraging, and he gave each of us individual advice. When I started, I could barely float, but now I can swim two full lengths of the pool without stopping.

However, there was one problem that affected almost every session. Because our class took place during open swim hours, the pool was often crowded, and we were usually given just one narrow lane. Several times we had to wait at the wall for minutes before we could practice.

For future courses, I would suggest scheduling the class at a quieter time, such as early on weekday evenings, or reserving at least two lanes for the group. Even a rope to separate the class area would make a big difference.

Best regards,
Grace

scenario: You have just moved to a new town and would like to volunteer at the local animal shelter on weekends. The shelter's website says new volunteers must attend an orientation but does not give dates or other details. You have experience caring for animals because your family fostered dogs for several years.
to: Ms. Kendra Moss, volunteer coordinator at Hillside Animal Shelter
subject: Interested in volunteering at the shelter
bullets: Introduce yourself and explain your interest.
Describe your experience with animals.
Ask about the orientation and other requirements.
sample_response:
Dear Ms. Moss,

My name is Jonah, and I recently moved to Hillside from Portland for a new job. I've been looking for a way to get involved in the community, and since I've always loved animals, volunteering at your shelter on weekends seems like the perfect fit.

I have quite a bit of hands-on experience. For about five years, my family fostered dogs for a rescue group, usually one or two at a time. I helped feed and walk them, gave them medicine when needed, and worked on basic training, such as walking on a leash. Some of them had been neglected, so I also learned how to be patient with nervous animals.

Your website mentions that new volunteers must attend an orientation, but I couldn't find any dates. Could you tell me when the next session will be held and how long it lasts? I'd also like to know whether volunteers must commit to a minimum number of hours.

Thank you for your time.

Best,
Jonah

scenario: Last week, you paid a bicycle shop $85 to repair the brakes on your bike, which you ride to work every day. When you picked it up, the brakes still squeaked loudly, and the next morning the rear brake barely worked on a steep hill. The shop's owner, Mr. Diaz, was not there when you called.
to: Mr. Roberto Diaz, owner of Diaz Cycle Repair
subject: Brakes still not working after repair
bullets: Describe the repair you paid for.
Explain what went wrong afterward.
Say what you would like the shop to do.
sample_response:
Dear Mr. Diaz,

I am writing about the brake repair your shop did on my blue commuter bike last Wednesday. I paid $85 for the work, which, according to my receipt, included new brake pads and an adjustment of both brakes. Since I ride this bike to work every day, I was relieved to have it fixed quickly.

Unfortunately, the problem has not been solved. When I picked the bike up, both brakes were still squeaking loudly. Even worse, the next morning, as I was riding down the steep hill on Clark Street, the rear brake barely slowed me down. I had to put my feet on the ground to stop safely, which was quite frightening.

I would like the shop to inspect the bike again and complete the repair properly at no additional cost. I can bring it in this Saturday morning. As I depend on the bike for my commute, I would appreciate it if the work could be finished the same day.

Sincerely,
Claire

scenario: Last weekend, you visited your friend Emma's hometown, and her parents, Mr. and Mrs. Larsen, let you stay in their guest room. They showed you around the town and cooked a delicious fish stew. You want to thank them, and you would love to make the stew yourself.
to: Mr. and Mrs. Larsen, your friend's parents
subject: Thank you for a wonderful weekend
bullets: Thank them for their hospitality.
Mention a highlight of your visit.
Ask them to share the recipe for the stew.
sample_response:
Dear Mr. and Mrs. Larsen,

Thank you so much for welcoming me into your home last weekend. From the moment I arrived, you made me feel like part of the family. The guest room was so comfortable that I slept better than I have in months, and I really appreciated you taking the time to show me around.

The highlight of my visit was definitely Saturday afternoon. Walking along the harbor, hearing the story of how the old lighthouse was saved, and then watching the sunset from the hill behind your house was unforgettable. Emma has always said her hometown is beautiful, but now I understand what she meant.

I also have a small favor to ask. I haven't stopped thinking about the fish stew you made on Saturday night! Would you be willing to share the recipe? I'd love to cook it for my roommates and tell them where it came from.

Thank you again for your kindness.

Warmest wishes,
Maya

scenario: You volunteer as an assistant coach for a team of ten-year-olds in a city youth basketball league. Many of the team's basketballs are worn out, and there are only six for fourteen players, so children spend much of practice waiting. The league coordinator, Mr. Banks, manages the equipment budget.
to: Mr. Terrence Banks, youth league coordinator
subject: Request for additional basketballs
bullets: Describe the current equipment situation.
Explain how it affects the players.
Make a specific request and explain how the equipment will be cared for.
sample_response:
Dear Mr. Banks,

I'm one of the volunteer assistant coaches for the Eastside Hawks, the under-eleven team that practices at Lincoln Gym on Tuesday and Thursday evenings. I'm writing to ask for help with our equipment.

At the moment, we have only six basketballs for fourteen players, and two of them are so worn that they barely bounce. As a result, during dribbling and shooting drills, more than half the kids end up standing in line instead of practicing. Some of the younger players get bored and lose focus, and they don't touch the ball often enough to improve.

Would it be possible for the league to provide eight new youth-size basketballs before the season starts in two weeks? I'll make sure they are labeled with the team name and stored in a locked bin at the gym after every practice. I'll also count them at the end of each session so none go missing.

Thank you for supporting the league.

Best regards,
Ryan

scenario: Your apartment building has a large lobby with an empty corner near the mailboxes. You have noticed that many residents enjoy reading, and you often see books left in the recycling bin. The building manager, Ms. Ortiz, recently asked residents for ideas to make the building feel more like a community.
to: Ms. Lucia Ortiz, building manager
subject: Idea for the lobby: a book swap shelf
bullets: Describe what you have noticed in the building.
Suggest your idea and explain how it would work.
Explain how it would benefit residents.
sample_response:
Dear Ms. Ortiz,

Thank you for inviting residents to share ideas about building a stronger community here. I have one suggestion that I think would be easy and inexpensive.

Over the past few months, I've noticed that many of our neighbors love to read. I often see people with novels on the benches outside, and almost every week there are perfectly good books thrown into the recycling bin. At the same time, the corner of the lobby next to the mailboxes is completely empty.

My idea is to set up a small book swap shelf in that corner. Residents could leave books they've finished and take any that interest them, with no sign-up or fees. I'd be happy to donate a bookcase and about twenty books to get it started, and to tidy the shelf once a week.

I believe it would reduce waste, save people money, and give neighbors a natural reason to chat with each other while checking their mail.

Kind regards,
Tomás

scenario: You are traveling in Portugal for two weeks to visit relatives. Yesterday, your bank card was declined at a supermarket and an ATM, and you discovered that the bank had blocked it because of "unusual foreign activity." Calling the bank from abroad is very expensive, so you decide to write through the bank's online messaging service.
to: Customer Service, Northgate Savings Bank
subject: Card blocked while traveling abroad
bullets: Explain what happened when you tried to use your card.
Describe your travel plans.
Ask the bank to unblock your card and prevent the problem from happening again.
sample_response:
Dear Customer Service Team,

I am writing because my debit card, ending in 4417, has been blocked while I am abroad. Yesterday afternoon, my payment was declined at a supermarket in Lisbon, and a few minutes later an ATM refused to give me cash. When I checked the banking app, I saw a message saying the card had been frozen because of unusual foreign activity.

I can confirm that these transactions were mine. I am in Portugal visiting relatives from June 3 to June 17, and during that time I will be staying in Lisbon and Porto. I forgot to notify the bank about my trip before I left, which I realize may have caused this.

Could you please unblock my card as soon as possible? I have very little cash and depend on the card for daily expenses. I would also be grateful if you could add a travel note to my account for these dates so that the card is not blocked again.

Thank you for your prompt assistance.

Sincerely,
Paulo Mendes

scenario: You are a summer intern at a software company. Every year, interns present their projects to company leaders at a final showcase, but your supervisor, Ms. Ferreira, has announced that this year's showcase is canceled to save time during a busy quarter. You and the other interns have worked for ten weeks on projects you hoped to present.
to: Ms. Diana Ferreira, intern program supervisor
subject: Reconsidering the intern showcase
bullets: Show that you understand the reason for her decision.
Explain why the showcase matters to the interns and to the company.
Propose a modified version of the event that requires less time.
sample_response:
Dear Ms. Ferreira,

Thank you for letting us know about the change to the end-of-summer schedule. I completely understand that this is an exceptionally busy quarter and that asking senior staff to give up an entire afternoon is difficult right now.

Still, I hope you might reconsider canceling the showcase altogether. For the twelve of us, it is the one opportunity to show leaders what we have built over ten weeks, and for interns hoping to return full-time, it is an important chance to be noticed. The company benefits too: last year, two intern prototypes were adopted by the product team after the showcase.

Would a shorter format be possible? Instead of formal presentations, we could hold a one-hour demo session during lunch in the main conference room. Leaders could drop by for as long as they had time, and we interns would handle all of the setup and catering arrangements ourselves.

I would be glad to coordinate the details if this sounds workable.

Best regards,
Kai

scenario: You broke your ankle playing soccer, and your doctor has told you not to exercise for eight weeks. Your gym allows members to freeze their membership, but its policy requires thirty days' written notice, which means you would have to pay for a month you cannot use. You have been a member for four years.
to: Mr. Steven Clarke, membership manager at Peak Fitness
subject: Request for an exception to the freeze policy
bullets: Explain your situation and why you need to freeze your membership.
Acknowledge the policy but explain why your case deserves an exception.
Propose specific terms for the freeze.
sample_response:
Dear Mr. Clarke,

I am writing to ask for your help with my Peak Fitness membership. Last Saturday, I broke my ankle during a soccer match, and my doctor has instructed me not to exercise for at least eight weeks. I have attached a copy of her note for your reference.

I understand that the gym requires thirty days' notice to freeze a membership, and I can see why that policy exists for planned breaks. However, my injury was sudden and completely unexpected, so giving advance notice was impossible. Under the standard rule, I would pay a full month's fee for a facility I physically cannot use. I have been a member for four years without missing a payment, and I hope that history can be taken into account.

Would you consider freezing my membership starting today, for nine weeks? I would be happy to pay the usual freeze fee of $10 per month, and I fully intend to return as soon as I recover.

Thank you for your understanding.

Sincerely,
Natalie

scenario: You work part-time at a print shop. Last week, you prepared 500 flyers for a local bakery's grand opening, but you accidentally typed the wrong phone number, and the owner, Mrs. Huang, has already handed out half of them. She called the shop, very upset, and your manager has asked you to write to her directly.
to: Mrs. Mei Huang, owner of Golden Crust Bakery
subject: Our mistake on your opening flyers
bullets: Apologize and take responsibility for the error.
Explain how the mistake happened.
Describe how the shop will fix the problem and make up for it.
sample_response:
Dear Mrs. Huang,

I am very sorry for the error on the flyers for your grand opening. I prepared the order myself, and the incorrect phone number was entirely my mistake. I understand how frustrating this must be, especially since you have already handed out so many of them.

When I typed the text from your order form, I reversed two digits in the number, and I did not ask you to check a final proof before printing. That step is normally part of our process, but because we were very busy that afternoon, I skipped it. I should not have done so.

To fix the problem, we will reprint all 500 flyers with the correct number free of charge, and they will be ready by noon tomorrow. My manager has also agreed to print 200 small correction cards for your counter and to give you 20 percent off your next order. From now on, I will send every customer a proof before printing.

With sincere apologies,
Jordan Lee
Bright Print Shop

scenario: You have been offered a three-month internship in another city this summer, but you still have eight months left on your apartment lease. Paying rent in two places would be very difficult. Your lease says subletting is not allowed without the landlord's approval, and your landlord, Ms. Bianchi, is known for being strict.
to: Ms. Francesca Bianchi, landlord
subject: Request to sublet my apartment this summer
bullets: Explain your situation and why you are asking.
Address concerns she might have about subletting.
Propose specific conditions for the arrangement.
sample_response:
Dear Ms. Bianchi,

I hope you are well. I am writing to request your approval for a short-term sublet of my apartment, unit 12, from June 1 to August 31. I have been offered a paid summer internship at an engineering firm in Denver, and paying rent in two cities for three months would be very difficult for me.

I understand that you may be concerned about having a stranger living in the building. That is why I would choose the subtenant very carefully. My preferred candidate is Clara Novak, a graduate student recommended by a colleague, who has excellent references and does not smoke or have pets.

I would propose the following conditions: you would meet Clara and approve her before anything is signed; I would remain fully responsible for the rent and for any damage; and she would follow every rule in the current lease. I could also pay an extra $500 deposit for the summer if that would give you more peace of mind.

Thank you for considering this.

Sincerely,
Ahmed

scenario: Your city council is considering a plan to turn half of Willow Park, the only green space in your neighborhood, into a parking lot for a new shopping center. Many families, older residents, and dog owners use the park daily. Council Member Rivera has invited residents to send written comments before the vote next month.
to: Council Member Angela Rivera, city council
subject: Concerns about the Willow Park parking proposal
bullets: Explain how you and others use the park.
Give reasons why the plan would harm the neighborhood.
Suggest an alternative way to meet the need for parking.
sample_response:
Dear Council Member Rivera,

Thank you for inviting residents to comment on the proposal for Willow Park. As someone who has lived on Birch Street for six years, I would like to share my concerns.

Willow Park is the heart of our neighborhood. I walk there every morning, and on weekends the playground is full of families, while older residents meet on the benches near the fountain. For many people in nearby apartments, it is the only place where they can enjoy trees and fresh air.

Turning half of it into a parking lot would harm the neighborhood in several ways. It would remove the only shaded area during hot summers, increase traffic next to the playground, and leave too little space for the community events held there each year.

I understand that the new shopping center needs parking. However, the empty lot behind the old post office on Fifth Avenue is only two blocks away. Building a parking garage on that site would meet the need without sacrificing our green space.

Respectfully,
Helen Brooks

scenario: Your close friend Omar has decided to open a food truck selling Middle Eastern street food, and he has asked you to become his business partner and invest $10,000 of your savings. You believe in his cooking, but you are saving for graduate school and do not want to take on the financial risk. You want to say no without hurting his feelings.
to: Omar, a close friend
subject: Re: The food truck plan
bullets: Tell him what you admire about his plan.
Explain your decision and the reasons for it.
Offer another way to support him.
sample_response:
Hi Omar,

I've been thinking about your message all week, and first of all, I'm honored that you'd want me as a partner. Your falafel wraps are the best I've ever had, and your plan to park near the office buildings at lunchtime and the stadium on game nights is genuinely smart. I have no doubt people will line up for your food.

That's why this has been hard to write. I've decided not to invest or become a partner. As you know, I'm saving for my master's program, which starts next fall, and that $10,000 is a big part of my tuition. If something unexpected happened with the truck, I'd be in a really difficult position, and I'd hate for money to ever come between us.

But I still want to help in any way I can. I could design your logo and menu, set up your social media accounts, and work at the truck on Saturdays during your first month. Just tell me where you need me.

Your friend always,
Sam

scenario: You work evening shifts at a restaurant with your coworker Jess, whom you like personally. For the past month, Jess has often left early or spent the last hour on her phone, leaving you to do most of the closing tasks alone. You would rather talk to her directly than complain to your manager.
to: Jess, coworker at the restaurant
subject: Our closing shifts
bullets: Explain the problem you have noticed without sounding accusatory.
Describe how it is affecting you.
Suggest a fair way to share the work.
sample_response:
Hi Jess,

I hope this doesn't come across the wrong way, because I really enjoy working with you. I wanted to message you directly instead of saying anything to Rachel, since I'm sure we can sort this out between us.

Lately, I've noticed that on our closing nights, I've been doing most of the end-of-shift tasks, like cleaning the kitchen, restocking, and counting the register. I know you've had a lot going on, and maybe you didn't realize how uneven it had become.

The problem is that closing alone takes me almost an hour longer, so I've been getting home after midnight several times a week. Since I also start work at a bakery at 7 a.m. most days, I'm exhausted, and honestly, I've started to feel a little resentful, which I don't want.

What if we made a checklist and split it in half? We could swap halves each week so nobody always gets the worst jobs, like mopping. And if something is making closing hard for you, I'm happy to talk about that too.

Thanks,
Mia

scenario: You booked a five-day vacation package through a travel agency that promised a "four-star beachfront hotel." When you arrived, the agency had moved you to a two-star hotel twenty minutes from the beach, without any explanation. The agency's local representative said she could do nothing and told you to write to the head office.
to: Customer Relations Manager, SunPath Travel
subject: Hotel downgrade on my vacation package
bullets: Describe what you booked and what you actually received.
Explain how the change affected your vacation.
State what compensation you believe is fair and why.
sample_response:
Dear Customer Relations Manager,

I am writing about my recent five-day package to Crete (booking reference SP-58214), from September 3 to 8. I paid $1,850 for a trip that promised accommodation at the Azure Bay Resort, which your brochure describes as a four-star beachfront hotel.

When I arrived, however, I was told I had been moved to the Hotel Kostas, a two-star property twenty minutes from the beach by bus. No one explained the change or apologized. The room was small, the air conditioning was unreliable, and the only restaurant closed at 8 p.m.

As a result, the relaxing beach holiday I had planned for months became a series of bus rides. I also spent about $120 on transportation and meals that would have been included at the original resort.

Since I received a far lower level of service than I paid for, I believe a refund of 40 percent of the package price, plus my additional costs, would be fair. I have kept all receipts and can send them on request.

Sincerely,
Laura Chen

scenario: Your manager at a nonprofit organization, Mr. Gordon, has asked staff to recommend candidates for a new volunteer coordinator position. You think your former coworker from a summer job, Leah, would be ideal, but she has less formal experience than the job description asks for. You want to make a convincing case for her.
to: Mr. Alan Gordon, program director
subject: Recommendation for the volunteer coordinator position
bullets: Introduce the person you are recommending and explain how you know her.
Explain why she would be a strong fit for the role.
Address the concern about her limited experience.
sample_response:
Dear Mr. Gordon,

Following your request for referrals, I would like to recommend Leah Osborne for the volunteer coordinator position. Leah and I worked together for two summers at Camp Redwood, where she supervised the volunteers in the arts and crafts program.

I believe Leah would be an excellent fit for three reasons. First, she is remarkably organized: she created a scheduling system that cut volunteer no-shows by about half. Second, she communicates warmly with people of all ages, so volunteers felt appreciated and kept coming back. Finally, she stays calm under pressure, which I saw firsthand when a storm forced us to relocate an event for 200 children in less than an hour.

I am aware that Leah has two years of experience, while the posting asks for three. However, the skills she developed in those two years match this role closely, and she learns new systems quickly. I am confident she would grow into the position faster than most candidates.

Kind regards,
Rebecca

scenario: Two weeks ago, a pipe burst in the apartment above yours, and water damaged several of your belongings, including two books you had borrowed from the public library. The library has charged you $90 to replace them. Your building's insurance will not cover the books, and you feel the charge is unfair since the damage was not your fault.
to: Ms. Patricia Wong, branch manager of Riverside Public Library
subject: Request to reduce charges for water-damaged books
bullets: Explain how the books were damaged.
Explain why you believe the full charge should be reconsidered.
Propose an alternative solution.
sample_response:
Dear Ms. Wong,

I am writing about the $90 replacement fee on my library account for two books, a cookbook and a travel guide to Japan. On October 2, a pipe burst in the apartment above mine, and water poured through my ceiling overnight. The two library books on my coffee table were soaked and are no longer usable. I have attached a letter from my building manager confirming the incident.

I fully accept that the library should not lose money because of what happened. However, the damage was not caused by any carelessness on my part, and unfortunately, my building's insurance does not cover borrowed items. I have used this library for over ten years and have always returned books on time.

Would it be possible for me to replace the books myself? I have found new copies of both titles online for about $45 in total. Alternatively, I would be glad to pay a reduced fee or to volunteer at the library to cover the difference.

Thank you for your consideration.

Sincerely,
Victor

scenario: You are the captain of a team in a recreational adult volleyball league. Last Sunday, your team was given a forfeit loss for not showing up, but the league's online schedule had listed the game at a different gym, where your team waited for an hour. The loss means your team will probably miss the playoffs.
to: Ms. Rachel Kim, recreational league director
subject: Appeal of Sunday's forfeit decision
bullets: Explain what happened on the day of the game.
Explain why you believe the decision is unfair.
Propose a solution that would be fair to both teams.
sample_response:
Dear Ms. Kim,

I am the captain of the Net Gains, and I am writing to appeal the forfeit loss our team received for last Sunday's 4 p.m. game against the Spikers.

On Sunday, all eight of our players arrived at Westside Recreation Center by 3:45 p.m., because that was the location listed on the league's online schedule. When no one else came, we called the league office but got no answer. We waited until after 5 p.m. before going home. Only later did we learn that the game had been moved to Central Gym.

I believe the forfeit is unfair because we followed the official schedule exactly. I saved a screenshot of the page from Saturday evening showing Westside as the venue, which I can send you. Since this loss will probably keep us out of the playoffs, the consequences are serious.

Would you consider canceling the forfeit and rescheduling the match for an open court time next week? We would gladly adapt to whatever time suits the Spikers.

Best regards,
Chris Ruiz

scenario: You have volunteered at a local food bank every Saturday for a year. Recently, many Saturday shifts have been badly understaffed because volunteers sign up by phone and often forget, while other shifts have too many people. The volunteer coordinator, Mr. Lee, is very busy and has asked experienced volunteers for help.
to: Mr. Jonathan Lee, food bank volunteer coordinator
subject: A proposal for scheduling Saturday volunteers
bullets: Describe the problem with the current system.
Propose a new system and explain how it would work.
Explain its benefits and respond to a possible concern about your idea.
sample_response:
Dear Mr. Lee,

I know you've been under a lot of pressure lately, so I'd like to offer an idea that might lighten your load. The phone sign-up system doesn't seem to be working well. Two weeks ago, only four of us showed up to sort a delivery that needed ten people, yet the following Saturday so many volunteers came that some just stood around.

I'd like to propose a free online sign-up sheet. Each Saturday would be divided into two shifts with a maximum number of spots, and volunteers would receive automatic email reminders two days before their shift. You could see at a glance which shifts need more people.

This would save you hours of phone calls and give us more balanced teams. I know some of our older volunteers may not be comfortable with computers, so I'd be happy to keep a paper list at the front desk and enter their names myself every week.

If you're interested, I could set up a trial version this month.

Best wishes,
Fatima

scenario: Your older brother, Ethan, has written to tell you he is thinking of quitting his stable accounting job to travel around South America for a year. He says he feels bored and stuck, but he has not saved much money. He has asked for your honest opinion, and you have mixed feelings about his plan.
to: Ethan, your older brother
subject: Re: Thinking about a big change
bullets: Show that you understand his feelings.
Give your honest opinion of the plan, including any concerns.
Suggest a practical alternative or next step.
sample_response:
Hey Ethan,

Thanks for trusting me with this. I could tell from your message how restless you've been, and honestly, I'm not surprised. You've been talking about seeing Machu Picchu since we were kids, and spending every day on spreadsheets you don't care about would wear anyone down.

Since you asked for my honest opinion, here it is: I love the idea of the trip, but I'm worried about the timing. If you quit now with only a few months of savings, you might have to come home early, or spend the whole year stressed about money instead of enjoying it. Finding another job afterward could also take a while.

What if you made a clear plan instead? You could save aggressively for the next eight months and, in the meantime, ask your firm whether they offer unpaid leave. Even a three-month trip could help you figure out whether you want to travel longer or change careers altogether.

Whatever you decide, I'm on your side.

Love,
Nora

scenario: The roots of a large oak tree in your neighbor Mr. Sullivan's yard have pushed over part of the wooden fence between your properties, and some branches now rest on your roof. A contractor has estimated that repairing the fence will cost $1,200. You get along well with Mr. Sullivan and want to share the costs fairly without starting a conflict.
to: Mr. Patrick Sullivan, neighbor
subject: The fence between our yards
bullets: Describe the damage and its cause tactfully.
Explain why the issue needs attention soon.
Propose a fair way to divide the work and the costs.
sample_response:
Dear Patrick,

I hope you and Margaret are enjoying the warmer weather. I wanted to write to you about something I noticed in the backyard, since I think it affects both of us.

After the heavy rain last week, about three meters of the fence between our yards started leaning badly. When I looked more closely, it seemed that the roots of your beautiful oak tree have gradually lifted the posts. Some of the larger branches are also now resting on the edge of my roof.

I'd like to deal with it fairly soon, because the fence could fall during the next storm, and my dog could easily get out into the street. The branches may also damage my gutters.

A contractor I trust estimated $1,200 to replace that section. Since the fence belongs to both of us, would you be willing to split the cost equally? In return, I'd be happy to arrange and pay for trimming the branches over my side. I'm free to talk over coffee anytime this week.

Best,
Simone

scenario: About three months ago, a phone repair shop replaced the cracked screen on your phone, and the work came with a 90-day warranty. Last week, the new screen began to flicker and stopped responding to touch, but the warranty had expired five days earlier. The shop's assistant said there was nothing he could do, so you are writing to the owner.
to: Mr. Hassan Karimi, owner of QuickFix Phone Repair
subject: Screen problem just after the warranty expired
bullets: Describe the repair and the problem that has developed.
Explain why you think the shop should still take responsibility.
Suggest a solution you would find acceptable.
sample_response:
Dear Mr. Karimi,

On March 2, your shop replaced the cracked screen on my phone for $160, and the repair came with a 90-day warranty. The screen worked well at first, but last week it began to flicker, and now the bottom third no longer responds to touch. I have not dropped the phone since the repair, and it has always been in a protective case.

When I visited the shop on Monday, your assistant explained that the warranty had expired five days earlier and that he could not help. I understand that warranties need a firm end date. However, a screen that fails after just over three months suggests that the part itself may have been defective. I chose your shop because of its excellent reputation, and I would like to keep recommending it to friends.

Would you be willing to replace the screen at cost, or at least to inspect the phone free of charge to find out what went wrong? I can bring it in any afternoon this week.

Sincerely,
Elena

scenario: Your six-month internship at an environmental consulting firm ended last week. Your supervisor, Dr. Morgan, gave you challenging projects and regular feedback. You are now applying for a full-time analyst position at another firm, and the application requires a reference from a recent supervisor within two weeks.
to: Dr. Susan Morgan, senior consultant and former internship supervisor
subject: Thank you, and a request for a reference
bullets: Thank her for her guidance during the internship.
Describe the job you are applying for and why her reference would be valuable.
Ask whether she would provide a reference and offer information to make it easier.
sample_response:
Dear Dr. Morgan,

Now that my internship has ended, I wanted to thank you properly for the past six months. You trusted me with real responsibility, such as the wetland survey for the Hanover project, and your weekly feedback helped me become a much more careful analyst. I especially appreciated the time you spent showing me how to present technical data to clients who are not scientists.

I am now applying for a full-time position as an environmental data analyst at GreenScope Consulting. The role focuses on water quality assessments, which is exactly the kind of work I did under your supervision. Because you saw my work firsthand, I believe your perspective would carry more weight than anyone else's.

Would you be willing to serve as a reference? The firm will contact references by email, and the deadline is May 20. If it would help, I would be happy to send you my résumé, the job description, and a short summary of the projects I completed.

With sincere thanks,
Ji-woo Park

scenario: Your friend Chloe lent you her expensive camera for your hiking trip. On the second day, you slipped on a wet rock and dropped it, and now the lens will not focus. You know the camera matters to her because she uses it for her part-time photography work.
to: Chloe, a close friend
subject: I'm so sorry about your camera
bullets: Apologize and explain what happened.
Show that you understand how this affects her.
Offer a concrete plan to make things right.
sample_response:
Hi Chloe,

I've been dreading writing this, but you deserve to hear it from me right away. I'm so sorry, but I damaged your camera on the trip. On Saturday morning, we were crossing a stream near the waterfall, and I slipped on a wet rock. I managed to catch myself, but the camera hit the stones, and now the lens won't focus at all.

I know this isn't just a camera to you. You need it for the wedding shoot next weekend, and I hate that my carelessness might put that job at risk. I also should have packed it away instead of keeping it around my neck while climbing.

Here's what I'd like to do. Tomorrow I'll take it to the repair shop on Main Street that you recommended, and I'll pay for the repair in full. If they can't fix it before your shoot, I'll rent you the same lens for the weekend. And if it can't be repaired, I'll replace it.

I'm really sorry.

Love,
Amelia
